questions.stem: About the layers of the heart wall:

options.label: A
options.text: The endocardium is lined by simple squamous epithelium

options.label: B
options.text: Purkinje fibres run in the subendocardial connective tissue

options.label: C
options.text: Cardiac muscle cells of the myocardium are arranged in a spiral fashion

options.label: D
options.text: The epicardium is the parietal layer of the serous pericardium

options.label: E
options.text: Coronary vessels and adipose tissue lie beneath the epicardial mesothelium

questions.why: False: D. It is the VISCERAL layer.

questions.stem: About the heart valves and conducting tissue:

options.label: A
options.text: The right atrioventricular valve has three cusps

options.label: B
options.text: The aortic and pulmonary semilunar valves each have two cusps

options.label: C
options.text: The SA node lies in the superior wall of the right atrium near the SVC opening

options.label: D
options.text: The bundle of His passes from the AV node into the interventricular septum

options.label: E
options.text: Purkinje fibres are small, thin cardiac muscle cells

notes.E: They are LARGE modified cardiac muscle cells.

questions.why: False: B, E. Each has THREE cusps. They are LARGE modified cardiac muscle cells.

questions.stem: The autonomic nerves to the heart:

options.label: A
options.text: initiate each heartbeat through the vagus nerves

options.label: B
options.text: modulate the heart rate but do not initiate it

options.label: C
options.text: reach the heart only from lower thoracic segments

options.label: D
options.text: are purely sympathetic, with no vagal supply

options.label: E
options.text: are absent from the atria and the conducting system

questions.why: The heartbeat starts in the SA node; sympathetic (upper thoracic) and vagal fibres only change the rate.

notes.A: The SA node initiates the beat.
notes.C: Sympathetic fibres come from UPPER thoracic segments.

questions.stem: Elastic (conducting) arteries:

options.label: A
options.text: include the aorta and its major branches

options.label: B
options.text: have a tunica media of smooth muscle separated by elastic lamellae

options.label: C
options.text: have a prominent, conspicuous internal elastic membrane

options.label: D
options.text: carry vasa vasorum in their adventitia and media

options.label: E
options.text: help smooth out the pressure changes produced by each heartbeat

notes.C: It is INCONSPICUOUS in elastic arteries.

questions.why: False: C. It is INCONSPICUOUS in elastic arteries.

questions.stem: Muscular (distributing) arteries:

options.label: A
options.text: include most of the named arteries of the body

options.label: B
options.text: have more elastin and less smooth muscle in the media than elastic arteries

options.label: C
options.text: show a prominent internal elastic lamina

options.label: D
options.text: may have an external elastic lamina at the media–adventitia boundary

questions.why: False: B, E. More smooth muscle, less elastin. Their adventitia contains vasa vasorum.

questions.stem: The fenestrated membranes found in the tunica media are characteristic of:
questions.why: Thick concentric fenestrated elastic membranes fill the media of elastic arteries.

questions.stem: A vessel whose wall thickness about equals its luminal diameter, with one or two smooth muscle layers, is most likely:
questions.why: Arterioles (10–100 µm) have up to two muscle layers and a lumen about equal to wall thickness.

notes.E: Scattered muscle, thin wall, wide lumen.

questions.stem: About metarterioles and precapillary sphincters:

options.label: A
options.text: Metarterioles arise from arterioles and give rise to capillaries

options.label: B
options.text: Metarterioles are surrounded by complete rings of smooth muscle

options.label: C
options.text: A precapillary sphincter is a single smooth muscle cell around a capillary origin

options.label: D
options.text: Constriction of the sphincters lets blood bypass the capillary bed

options.label: E
options.text: When the sphincters open, blood flows through the true capillaries

questions.why: False: B. INCOMPLETE rings.

questions.stem: About capillaries:

options.label: A
options.text: They are about 8–10 µm in diameter

options.label: B
options.text: They are usually less than 1 mm long

options.label: C
options.text: Their wall is a single layer of endothelium with a basal lamina

options.label: D
options.text: Pericytes form a continuous muscle coat around them

options.label: E
options.text: They form beds between arterioles and venules

questions.why: False: D. Pericytes are OCCASIONAL.

questions.stem: Capillary endothelial cells:

options.label: B
options.text: contain desmin and/or vimentin filaments around the nucleus

options.label: C
options.text: are joined mainly by fasciae occludentes

options.label: E
options.text: may enclose a lumen that admits one red cell at a time

notes.C: Tight junctions, with some desmosomes and gap junctions.

questions.why: False: D. They characteristically CONTAIN them.

questions.stem: Capillaries are classified mainly according to:

options.label: C
options.text: the number of pericytes around them

options.label: D
options.text: the organ and tissue that they supply

questions.why: Continuous, fenestrated and sinusoidal types differ in endothelium and basal lamina.

notes.C: Pericytes vary but do not define the types.
notes.D: Location follows the type, not the reverse.

questions.stem: Continuous (somatic) capillaries:

options.label: A
options.text: are typical of muscle, lung and the CNS

options.label: B
options.text: show occluding junctions in cross section

options.label: C
options.text: allow only small molecules (under about 10,000 Da) between cells

questions.why: False: D. That describes fenestrated capillaries.

questions.stem: Fenestrated (visceral) capillaries:

options.label: B
options.text: occur in the kidney, gut and gallbladder

options.label: D
options.text: may have a cartwheel-shaped diaphragm across the fenestration

options.label: E
options.text: in the gut, become thicker-walled during absorption

notes.D: With a central thickening and 14 wedge-shaped gaps.
notes.E: They THIN and gain fenestrations during absorption.

questions.why: False: E. They THIN and gain fenestrations during absorption.

questions.stem: The diaphragm across a capillary fenestration is thought to derive from:

options.label: B
options.text: the glycocalyx of a pinocytotic vesicle

questions.why: It comes from glycocalyx once enclosed in the vesicle that formed the fenestration.

questions.stem: Discontinuous (sinusoidal) capillaries:

options.label: A
options.text: are found in the liver, spleen and bone marrow

options.label: B
options.text: are narrower and more regular than other capillaries

options.label: C
options.text: may have a partial or absent basal lamina

options.label: D
options.text: in the liver are associated with Kupffer cells and Ito cells

options.label: E
options.text: in the spleen have spindle-shaped endothelial cells with gaps between them

questions.why: False: B. LARGER and more irregular.

questions.stem: Pericytes are regulated mainly by:
questions.why: Pericytes are contractile and respond to endothelial NO.

notes.D: A local mediator but not the stated control.
notes.E: Circulating hormone, not the stated control.

questions.stem: Arteriovenous shunts:

options.label: A
options.text: connect arteries to veins directly, bypassing capillaries

options.label: B
options.text: are common in the skin of the fingertips, nose and lips

options.label: D
options.text: mainly serve thermoregulation at the body surface

options.label: E
options.text: are the main site of gas exchange in the skin

notes.E: Exchange occurs in capillaries, which shunts bypass.

questions.why: False: E. Exchange occurs in capillaries, which shunts bypass.

questions.stem: About venules:

options.label: A
options.text: They include postcapillary and muscular venules

options.label: B
options.text: Postcapillary venules have the loosest endothelial junctions of the microvasculature

options.label: C
options.text: Leucocytes leave the circulation mainly at postcapillary venules

options.label: D
options.text: Their diameter may be as small as 0.1 mm

questions.why: False: E. Venules have no valves.

questions.stem: Medium veins:

options.label: A
options.text: include the radial, tibial and popliteal veins

options.label: B
options.text: have a diameter of up to about 10 mm

options.label: C
options.text: have valves, most numerous in the lower limbs

options.label: D
options.text: have a tunica media thicker than that of a medium artery

options.label: E
options.text: have an adventitia usually thicker than the media

questions.why: False: D. THINNER.

questions.stem: Large veins:

options.label: A
options.text: include the venae cavae, subclavian and hepatic portal veins

options.label: B
options.text: have a diameter greater than about 10 mm

options.label: C
options.text: have the adventitia as the thickest layer

options.label: D
options.text: have a sharp boundary between intima and media

options.label: E
options.text: contain longitudinal smooth muscle in the adventitia

questions.why: False: D. There is NO clear boundary.

questions.stem: Which layer is thickest in the wall of a large vein?
questions.why: The adventitia, with collagen, elastic fibres and longitudinal smooth muscle, is thickest.

questions.stem: Atypical blood vessels:

options.label: A
options.text: Coronary arteries are classed as medium-sized muscular arteries

options.label: B
options.text: Coronary artery walls are thinner than comparable limb arteries

options.label: C
options.text: Dural venous sinuses are lined by endothelium and lack smooth muscle

options.label: D
options.text: The great saphenous vein has a thick circular muscle coat in its media

options.label: E
options.text: The great saphenous vein has a well-developed internal elastic membrane

notes.B: THICKER, due to more circular smooth muscle.
notes.E: It is thin and poorly developed.

questions.why: False: B, E. THICKER, due to more circular smooth muscle. It is thin and poorly developed.

questions.stem: Atherosclerosis in the coronary arteries restricting oxygen supply to the myocardium leads to:
questions.why: Answer: B.

notes.C: Venous disease of the lower limb.

questions.stem: Lymphatic vessels:

options.label: B
options.text: are less permeable than blood capillaries

options.label: C
options.text: have valves and carry lymph in one direction

options.label: D
options.text: drain mainly into the thoracic duct on the left

options.label: E
options.text: pass through lymph nodes before lymph returns to the blood

notes.B: MORE permeable; they collect protein-rich fluid.

questions.why: False: B. MORE permeable; they collect protein-rich fluid.

questions.stem: Which vessel normally has 3–10 layers of smooth muscle and no vasa vasorum?
questions.why: From the comparison table: small arteries (0.1–1 mm).

notes.B: Many muscle layers; vasa vasorum may be present.

questions.stem: The vessel described as the major determinant of systemic blood pressure is the:
questions.why: Arterioles resist and control flow into capillary beds.

questions.stem: From the comparison table of vessels:

options.label: A
options.text: Capillaries have endothelium with pericytes only, and no adventitia

options.label: B
options.text: Venules are the main site of leucocyte exit from the vessels

options.label: C
options.text: Small veins have 2–3 loose smooth muscle layers in the media

options.label: D
options.text: Medium veins have 3–5 distinct smooth muscle layers

options.label: E
options.text: Elastic arteries have an adventitia thicker than the media

questions.why: False: E. Thinner than the media.

questions.stem: Which layer of the heart wall contains the Purkinje fibres?
questions.why: Purkinje fibres run in the subendocardial connective tissue, just under the endothelium.

notes.D: Dense connective tissue for valve attachment.

questions.stem: The coronary vessels and most of the cardiac adipose tissue lie in the:
questions.why: They lie under the mesothelium of the epicardium.

questions.stem: Compared with ordinary cardiac muscle cells, Purkinje fibres are:

options.label: A
options.text: larger and paler, with fewer myofibrils

options.label: B
options.text: smaller and darker, with more myofibrils

options.label: C
options.text: thinner, with central rows of nuclei

questions.why: They are large, glycogen-rich cells with sparse peripheral myofibrils.

questions.stem: Which feature best identifies an elastic artery in a section stained for elastin?

options.label: A
options.text: A single wavy internal elastic lamina

options.label: C
options.text: An adventitia thicker than the media

options.label: D
options.text: Longitudinal smooth muscle in the adventitia

questions.why: The media of the aorta is filled with fenestrated elastic membranes.

questions.stem: In a muscular artery, the most prominent elastic structure is the:
questions.why: It shows as a wavy, refractile line between intima and media.

notes.A: Present only in larger ones and thinner.

questions.stem: The vasa vasorum supply:

options.label: A
options.text: the outer wall of large vessels

questions.why: Large vessel walls are too thick to be nourished from the lumen alone.

questions.stem: Blood bypasses a capillary bed through the thoroughfare channel when:
questions.why: Closed sphincters send flow straight from the metarteriole to the venule.

notes.B: Pericytes do not route flow this way.

questions.stem: Which capillary type allows only small molecules to pass, mainly by pinocytotic transport?
questions.why: Continuous capillaries have tight junctions and an intact basal lamina.

questions.stem: Capillaries of the brain differ from other continuous capillaries in that they:

options.label: C
options.text: have wide gaps between endothelial cells

options.label: E
options.text: have Kupffer cells in their walls

questions.why: This underlies the blood–brain barrier.

questions.stem: The glomerulus of the kidney contains capillaries that are:
questions.why: Glomerular fenestrations lack diaphragms, but the basal lamina is thick.

notes.D: The glomerular basal lamina is thick.

questions.stem: Kupffer cells are found in the sinusoids of the:
questions.why: Resident macrophages of the liver sinusoids.

questions.stem: Ito (stellate) cells in the liver are specialised to:
questions.why: They lie in the space of Disse.

questions.stem: Oedema in acute inflammation results mainly from leakage at the:
questions.why: Their junctions are the loosest and open further under histamine.

questions.stem: Valves in veins are formed by folds of the:
questions.why: Endothelium-covered folds of intima with a little connective tissue.

questions.stem: Which vessel has the thinnest wall relative to the size of its lumen?
questions.why: Veins have thin walls and wide lumens.

questions.stem: A vessel shows a large lumen and a thick adventitia with longitudinal bundles of smooth muscle. It is most likely the:
questions.why: Large veins: adventitia thickest, with longitudinal smooth muscle.

questions.stem: The great saphenous vein is unusual because it has a:

options.label: A
options.text: thick, circular muscle coat in the media

options.label: B
options.text: fenestrated elastic membrane in the media

questions.why: Suited to high pressure in a dependent vein; useful as a bypass graft.

notes.C: It is thin and poorly developed.

questions.stem: The dural venous sinuses are best described as:

options.label: C
options.text: muscular veins with an elastic lamina

questions.why: They lie between layers of dura.

questions.stem: Lymphatic capillaries differ from blood capillaries in that they:

options.label: A
options.text: begin blindly with a patchy basal lamina

options.label: B
options.text: have a thick basal lamina and pericytes

options.label: C
options.text: carry red cells and platelets in lymph

questions.why: They are very permeable and take up protein-rich fluid.

notes.C: Lymph has no red cells normally.

questions.stem: The atrioventricular bundle (of His) runs into the:
questions.why: From the AV node it enters the septum and divides into right and left branches.

questions.stem: About the zones of the airway:

options.label: A
options.text: The conducting zone warms, moistens and filters inspired air

options.label: B
options.text: The trachea is generation 0 and the main bronchi generation 1

options.label: C
options.text: Terminal bronchioles belong to the respiratory zone

notes.C: They are the END of the conducting zone (generations 11–16).

questions.why: False: C. They are the END of the conducting zone (generations 11–16).

questions.stem: Which function is NOT listed for the respiratory system?
questions.why: Erythropoietin comes mainly from the kidney.

notes.B: Listed: ACE converts angiotensin I to II.

questions.stem: In the conducting airways:

options.label: E
options.text: the epithelium rests on a thin basement membrane in the trachea

notes.E: The tracheal basement membrane is THICK.

questions.why: False: E. The tracheal basement membrane is THICK.

questions.stem: Cells of the respiratory epithelium:

options.label: A
options.text: Goblet cells secrete mucus that traps particles and absorbs water-soluble gases

options.label: B
options.text: Ciliated cells move mucus toward the pharynx

options.label: C
options.text: Brush cells are chemosensory, with afferent nerve endings at their base

options.label: D
options.text: Small granule (K) cells are the stem cells of the epithelium

options.label: E
options.text: Small granule cells contain serotonin, calcitonin and bombesin

notes.D: BASAL cells are the stem cells; K cells are neuroendocrine.

questions.why: False: D. BASAL cells are the stem cells; K cells are neuroendocrine.

questions.stem: Cigarette smoking changes the respiratory mucosa mainly by:

options.label: A
options.text: loss of all goblet cells in the airway

options.label: B
options.text: increasing goblet cell number and size

options.label: E
options.text: replacing basal cells with brush cells

questions.why: Metaplastic change with more and bigger goblet cells and more secretion.

questions.stem: The olfactory epithelium:

options.label: A
options.text: is pseudostratified columnar without goblet cells

options.label: B
options.text: contains bipolar olfactory neurons with non-motile cilia

options.label: C
options.text: has sustentacular cells that make odorant-binding proteins

options.label: D
options.text: has the nuclei of sustentacular cells nearest the basement membrane

options.label: E
options.text: has olfactory receptor cells that live about one month

notes.D: They lie near the APEX; basal cell nuclei are basal.

questions.why: False: D. They lie near the APEX; basal cell nuclei are basal.

questions.stem: Bowman's glands of the olfactory mucosa function mainly to:

options.label: A
options.text: secrete mucus that traps dust particles

options.label: B
options.text: dissolve odorants and wash them away

options.label: E
options.text: warm the inspired air by heat exchange

questions.why: Their watery secretion dissolves odorants and then clears them.

notes.A: Goblet cells, which are absent here.

questions.stem: Epithelia of the upper airways:

options.label: A
options.text: The nasal vestibule has keratinised stratified squamous epithelium

options.label: C
options.text: The oropharynx has stratified squamous non-keratinised epithelium

options.label: D
options.text: Paranasal sinuses have thicker epithelium with more goblet cells than the nose

options.label: E
options.text: The laryngopharynx has stratified squamous non-keratinised epithelium

notes.D: Thinner, with FEWER goblet cells and glands.

questions.why: False: D. Thinner, with FEWER goblet cells and glands.

questions.stem: The larynx:

options.label: A
options.text: The false vocal folds have respiratory epithelium and seromucous glands

options.label: B
options.text: The true vocal folds have stratified squamous non-keratinised epithelium

options.label: C
options.text: The vocal ligament is made of parallel elastic fibres

options.label: D
options.text: Reinke's space is rich in lymphatics and blood vessels

options.label: E
options.text: The vocalis muscle is skeletal muscle

notes.D: It LACKS lymphatics and is poorly vascular (hence Reinke oedema).

questions.why: False: D. It LACKS lymphatics and is poorly vascular (hence Reinke oedema).

questions.stem: The epiglottis:

options.label: A
options.text: has stratified squamous epithelium on its lingual surface

options.label: B
options.text: shows a transition to respiratory epithelium on its posterior surface

options.label: D
options.text: has a lamina propria of loose areolar tissue

questions.why: False: D. DENSE irregular connective tissue.

questions.stem: The trachea:

options.label: A
options.text: has four layers: mucosa, submucosa, cartilage and adventitia

options.label: C
options.text: has the trachealis (smooth) muscle between the open ends of the rings

options.label: D
options.text: has a trachealis that contracts during swallowing

options.label: E
options.text: has seromucous glands in its submucosa

notes.D: It RELAXES so the oesophagus can bulge into the trachea.

questions.why: False: D. It RELAXES so the oesophagus can bulge into the trachea.

questions.stem: Bronchi are best identified histologically by:

options.label: A
options.text: C-shaped cartilage rings and trachealis muscle

options.label: B
options.text: cartilage plates and a circular smooth muscle layer

options.label: C
options.text: club cells and the absence of glands

questions.why: Answer: B.

questions.stem: Bronchi:

options.label: A
options.text: have five layers including a muscularis

options.label: B
options.text: have a submucosa thinner than that of the trachea

options.label: C
options.text: may have myoepithelial cells in their glands

options.label: E
options.text: have a thin basement membrane under the epithelium

questions.why: False: D. IRREGULAR discontinuous plates.

questions.stem: Bronchioles:

options.label: B
options.text: have the highest proportion of smooth muscle in the bronchial tree

options.label: C
options.text: have goblet cells right down to the terminal bronchioles

options.label: D
options.text: have club (Clara) cells in terminal and respiratory bronchioles

options.label: E
options.text: have three layers: mucosa, muscularis and adventitia

notes.C: Goblet cells are absent from terminal bronchioles.

questions.why: False: C. Goblet cells are absent from terminal bronchioles.

questions.stem: Club (Clara) cells:

options.label: C
options.text: act as stem cells for the bronchiolar epithelium

options.label: E
options.text: are found mainly in the trachea and main bronchi

questions.why: False: E. Only in BRONCHIOLES.

questions.stem: Respiratory bronchioles differ from terminal bronchioles mainly by:
questions.why: Answer: B.

questions.stem: About alveoli:

options.label: A
options.text: Each adult lung has about 150–250 million alveoli

options.label: B
options.text: Each alveolus is about 0.2 mm in diameter

options.label: C
options.text: The total surface area is about 75 m²

options.label: D
options.text: Alveoli communicate through pores of Kohn

options.label: E
options.text: Pores of Kohn prevent the spread of pneumonia between alveoli

questions.why: False: E. They FACILITATE its spread.

questions.stem: Type I pneumocytes:

options.label: B
options.text: make up about 40% of alveolar cells

options.label: C
options.text: cover about 95% of the alveolar surface

options.label: E
options.text: can divide to replace lost alveolar cells

notes.E: They are NOT capable of division.

questions.why: False: D, E. Type II cells make surfactant. They are NOT capable of division.

questions.stem: Type II pneumocytes:

options.label: A
options.text: are large cuboidal cells that bulge into the air space

options.label: C
options.text: secrete surfactant that lowers surface tension

options.label: D
options.text: can divide to form type I and type II cells

options.label: E
options.text: decrease in number as a marker of alveolar injury

questions.why: False: E. HYPERPLASIA marks injury and repair.

questions.stem: Alveolar macrophages:

options.label: A
options.text: lie in the septa or within the alveoli

options.label: C
options.text: are called heart failure cells when they ingest leaked blood

options.label: D
options.text: derive from monocytes that migrate into the lung

questions.why: False: E. Their apoptosis CONTRIBUTES to emphysema.

questions.stem: Which is NOT part of the blood–air barrier?
questions.why: Barrier: surfactant, type I cell, fused basal laminae, endothelium.

notes.E: Usually counted as the innermost lining.

questions.stem: In emphysema, the alveolar walls are destroyed mainly by:

options.label: C
options.text: collapse of the pores of Kohn

questions.why: Neutrophil proteases digest elastic and other fibres, increasing compliance.

notes.D: Type I cells do not divide.

questions.stem: From the summary table:

options.label: A
options.text: The tertiary bronchus has simple columnar epithelium

options.label: B
options.text: The trachea has the most glands and cartilage

options.label: C
options.text: Club cells are absent from the trachea and bronchi

options.label: D
options.text: Respiratory bronchioles have abundant goblet cells

options.label: E
options.text: Alveolar ducts are lined by simple squamous epithelium

questions.why: False: D. Absent.

questions.stem: An immotile-cilia syndrome affecting the airways is:
questions.why: Primary ciliary dyskinesia.

notes.A: Thick mucus from a chloride channel defect.

questions.stem: The respiratory zone of the airway begins at the:
questions.why: Respiratory bronchioles (gen. 17–19) are the first with alveoli in their walls.

options.label: D
options.text: simple squamous with type I cells

questions.why: This is "respiratory epithelium", nasal cavity to bronchi.

questions.stem: The stem cells of the respiratory epithelium are the:
questions.why: Basal cells sit on the basement membrane and replace other cells.

questions.stem: Cells of the respiratory epithelium containing serotonin, calcitonin and bombesin are:
questions.why: Part of the diffuse neuroendocrine system.

questions.stem: Brush cells of the respiratory epithelium are thought to be:

questions.stem: The olfactory receptor cells are:

options.label: D

questions.why: Their axons form the olfactory nerve; they are replaced about monthly.

questions.stem: Reinke oedema develops easily because the superficial lamina propria of the true vocal fold:

questions.stem: The epithelium of the true vocal fold is:
questions.why: It resists the friction of vibration.

questions.stem: The cartilage of the epiglottis is:

questions.stem: Bronchioles are distinguished from bronchi by:

options.label: A
options.text: type I cell and endothelial basal laminae fuse

options.text: type II cells overlie the capillary

options.text: club cells line the alveolar duct

options.text: allow infection to spread between alveoli

questions.stem: About the oral cavity:

options.label: A
options.text: The vestibule lies between the teeth or gums and the lips or cheeks

options.label: B
options.text: The vestibule and oral cavity proper communicate at the retromolar region

options.label: C
options.text: The roof of the oral cavity proper is the palate

options.label: D
options.text: Its floor is supported by geniohyoid and mylohyoid

options.label: E
options.text: It is continuous behind with the nasopharynx

notes.E: With the OROpharynx, through the fauces.

questions.why: False: E. With the OROpharynx, through the fauces.

questions.stem: Types of oral mucosa:

options.label: A
options.text: Masticatory mucosa makes up about 25% and is usually keratinised

options.label: B
options.text: Lining mucosa makes up about 60% and is non-keratinised

options.label: C
options.text: Specialised mucosa makes up about 15% and covers the dorsum of the tongue

options.label: D
options.text: The hard palate is covered by lining mucosa

options.label: E
options.text: The soft palate is covered by lining mucosa

questions.why: False: D. MASTICATORY mucosa.

questions.stem: Which site is covered by lining mucosa?
questions.why: Answer: C.

questions.stem: Lining mucosa:

options.label: B
options.text: has fewer and shorter connective tissue papillae

options.label: C
options.text: has a distinct submucosa everywhere, including under the tongue

options.label: D
options.text: has numerous deep papillae in the alveolar mucosa

notes.B: Because of movement of the underlying muscle.
notes.C: No submucosa under the INFERIOR surface of the tongue.

questions.why: False: C. No submucosa under the INFERIOR surface of the tongue.

questions.stem: Masticatory mucosa:

options.label: B
options.text: has long, numerous epithelial ridges and connective tissue papillae

options.label: C
options.text: lacks a submucosa in the midline of the hard palate

options.label: D
options.text: covers the gingiva and hard palate

options.label: E
options.text: is soft and pliable to allow movement

questions.why: False: E. That describes lining mucosa.

questions.stem: In parakeratinised epithelium, the surface cells:

options.label: A
options.text: are flat squames without any nuclei

questions.why: Parakeratinised squames keep pyknotic nuclei; it is commonest in the gingiva.

questions.stem: Fordyce spots are:

options.label: A
options.text: minor salivary glands of the lip

options.label: C
options.text: enlarged fungiform papillae of the lip

questions.why: Found near the angle of the mouth and in the cheeks opposite the molars.

questions.stem: The lip:

options.label: A
options.text: has orbicularis oris as its muscular core

options.label: B
options.text: has an inner mucous surface with keratinised epithelium

options.label: C
options.text: has a vermilion zone covered by very thin keratinised epithelium

options.label: D
options.text: has no salivary or sweat glands in the vermilion zone

options.label: E
options.text: has hair follicles, sebaceous and sweat glands on its outer surface

notes.D: It is kept moist by saliva.

questions.why: False: B. NON-keratinised, with labial salivary glands.

questions.stem: The pink colour of the vermilion zone of the lip is due to:
questions.why: Answer: B.

questions.stem: The tongue:

options.label: A
options.text: is made of skeletal muscle interspersed with glands

options.label: B
options.text: has muscles running in three planes at right angles

options.label: C
options.text: has a dorsum divided by the sulcus terminalis into anterior 2/3 and posterior 1/3

options.label: D
options.text: has the foramen caecum at the apex of the sulcus terminalis

options.label: E
options.text: carries lingual papillae mainly behind the sulcus terminalis

notes.E: Papillae lie IN FRONT of the sulcus.

questions.why: False: E. Papillae lie IN FRONT of the sulcus.

questions.stem: Filiform papillae:

options.label: B
options.text: are covered by highly keratinised epithelium

questions.why: False: C. They have NO taste buds.

questions.stem: Fungiform papillae:

options.label: B
options.text: are most numerous near the tip of the tongue

options.label: C
options.text: have taste buds on their dorsal surface

options.label: D
options.text: appear as red spots in children

questions.why: False: E. That describes circumvallate papillae.

questions.stem: Circumvallate papillae:

options.label: B
options.text: lie just in front of the sulcus terminalis

options.label: C
options.text: project well above the surface of the tongue

options.label: D
options.text: have taste buds on the lateral walls of the furrow

options.label: E
options.text: receive serous secretion from von Ebner's glands

notes.C: They do NOT protrude; a deep furrow surrounds them.

questions.why: False: C. They do NOT protrude; a deep furrow surrounds them.

questions.stem: Which papillae have taste buds that degenerate shortly after the 2nd year of life?
questions.why: Foliate papillae lie on the lateral edge of the tongue.

questions.stem: Taste buds:

options.label: A
options.text: occur on fungiform, foliate and circumvallate papillae

options.label: B
options.text: are pale-staining oval bodies through the epithelium

options.label: D
options.text: have gustatory cells as the least numerous cells

options.label: E
options.text: have basal cells that act as stem cells

notes.D: Gustatory (sensory) cells are the MOST numerous.

questions.why: False: D. Gustatory (sensory) cells are the MOST numerous.

questions.stem: Which taste bud cells do NOT synapse with nerve fibres?

options.label: E
options.text: Cells that reach the taste pore and synapse

questions.why: Supporting cells reach the pore but do not synapse.

questions.stem: Enamel:

options.label: E
options.text: ends at the neck at the cementoenamel junction

questions.why: False: C. It is ACELLULAR.

questions.stem: The neonatal line in deciduous enamel marks:

options.label: A
options.text: the change from prenatal to postnatal nutrition

options.label: B
options.text: the eruption of the first permanent molar

options.label: E
options.text: the junction of enamel and cementum

questions.why: Answer: A.

questions.stem: Dentin:

options.label: A
options.text: forms the bulk of the crown and root

options.label: D
options.text: is made by odontoblasts only before eruption

options.label: E
options.text: contains odontoblast processes in dentinal tubules

questions.why: False: D. Odontoblasts make dentin THROUGHOUT LIFE.

questions.stem: Cementum and pulp:

options.label: D
options.text: The pulp is loose connective tissue rich in vessels and nerves

options.label: E
options.text: Vessels and nerves enter the pulp through the apical foramen

questions.why: False: B. It is AVASCULAR.

questions.stem: Serous and mucous acini:

options.label: C
options.text: Mucous cells have flat, peripheral nuclei

options.label: D
options.text: Mucous acini stain darkly with H&E

options.label: E
options.text: Serous demilunes are thought to be fixation artifacts

questions.why: False: D. They stain LIGHTLY.

questions.stem: Striated ducts of salivary glands:

options.label: A
options.text: are lined by low cuboidal cells and secrete HCO₃⁻

options.label: B
options.text: have basal infoldings with elongated mitochondria

options.label: C
options.text: are best developed in predominantly mucous glands

options.label: D
options.text: are lined by stratified columnar epithelium

options.label: E
options.text: add sodium and chloride to the saliva

questions.why: They pump out Na⁺ and Cl⁻ and add K⁺ and HCO₃⁻, making saliva hypotonic.

questions.stem: The functional unit of a salivary gland (the salivon) consists of the acinus with its:
questions.why: Answer: B.

questions.stem: Final saliva:

options.label: B
options.text: starts as a plasma-like fluid secreted by the acini

options.label: C
options.text: is made hypotonic because the ducts absorb water

options.label: D
options.text: has a high Na⁺/K⁺ ratio in hypoaldosteronism

options.label: E
options.text: has its secretion rate changed by aldosterone and ADH

notes.C: The ducts are relatively IMPERMEABLE to water.

questions.why: False: C, E. The ducts are relatively IMPERMEABLE to water. They alter COMPOSITION, not rate.

questions.stem: The parotid gland:
questions.why: False: E. About 20–25%; the submandibular gives most.

questions.stem: The submandibular gland:

options.label: A
options.text: is a mixed, predominantly serous gland

options.label: B
options.text: has mucous units capped with demilunes

options.label: C
options.text: drains by Wharton's duct at the sublingual caruncle

options.label: D
options.text: produces most of the unstimulated saliva

questions.why: False: E. It has striated ducts.

questions.stem: The sublingual gland:

options.label: A
options.text: is the smallest paired major gland

options.label: C
options.text: has few intercalated and rare striated ducts

options.label: D
options.text: drains by a single large duct opening opposite the upper molar

options.label: E
options.text: is the commonest site of ranulas

notes.D: Many small ducts; some join the submandibular duct.

questions.why: False: D. Many small ducts; some join the submandibular duct.

questions.stem: Pleomorphic adenoma most commonly affects the:
questions.why: About 85% parotid, 5% submandibular, 10% minor glands.

questions.stem: Salivary calculi (sialolithiasis) occur most often in the:
questions.why: Answer: B.

questions.stem: Waldeyer's tonsillar ring includes the:

notes.A: Between the palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches.

questions.why: False: E. Not part of the ring.

questions.stem: Minor salivary glands:

options.label: A
options.text: lie in the submucosa and open by short ducts

options.label: B
options.text: are compound glands with long main ducts

options.label: C
options.text: are found only in the lips and cheeks

options.label: D
options.text: secrete only under strong nervous stimulation

options.label: E
options.text: are absent from the palate and tongue

questions.why: Named by site: buccal, labial, lingual, palatine.

questions.stem: The vestibule communicates with the oral cavity proper when the teeth are clenched through the:
questions.why: The gap behind the last molars.

questions.stem: The mucosa of the hard palate differs from that of the cheek because it is:

options.label: A
options.text: keratinised and firmly bound to bone

questions.why: Masticatory mucosa resists friction during chewing.

questions.stem: The most common type of keratinisation in the gingiva is:
questions.why: The surface squames keep pyknotic nuclei.

questions.stem: The muscular core of the lip is the:
questions.why: Skeletal muscle encircling the mouth.

notes.E: Upper lip elevator, not the core.

questions.stem: The vermilion zone of the lip needs moistening by saliva because it:

options.label: A
options.text: has no salivary or sweat glands

options.label: D
options.text: has many sebaceous glands that dry it

questions.why: It has very thin keratin and a rich capillary bed.

questions.stem: The tongue is described as musculoglandular because it is made of:

options.label: A
options.text: skeletal muscle with glands between fibres

options.label: C
options.text: skeletal muscle covered by glandular skin

questions.why: Muscle bundles run in three planes, with glands among them.

questions.stem: The foramen caecum of the tongue marks the:

options.label: D
options.text: end of the circumvallate papillae row

questions.why: At the apex of the V-shaped sulcus terminalis.

notes.D: They lie in front of the sulcus.

questions.stem: Which papillae give the dorsum of the tongue its rough texture and have no taste buds?
questions.why: Most numerous, highly keratinised, mechanical role.

questions.stem: Von Ebner's glands are associated with the:
questions.why: Their serous secretion flushes the furrow and provides lingual lipase.

questions.stem: Which taste bud cells act as stem cells?
questions.why: They lie at the base of the bud.

questions.stem: The hardest tissue of the body, made mostly of hydroxyapatite, is:
questions.why: About 96–98% mineral, made by ameloblasts.

questions.stem: Dentin can be repaired throughout life because:
questions.why: Their processes run in dentinal tubules.

questions.stem: Cementocytes most closely resemble:
questions.why: Cementum is bone-like but avascular.

questions.stem: Serous acinar cells can be recognised by their:

options.label: B
options.text: flat nuclei pressed to the base

questions.why: Round basal nuclei with rough ER below and granules above.

questions.stem: Myoepithelial cells in salivary glands function to:

options.label: A
options.text: squeeze secretion out of the acini

options.label: E
options.text: form the capsule of the gland

questions.why: They lie between the secretory cells and the basal lamina.

questions.stem: Intercalated ducts are best developed in the:
questions.why: They are long and numerous in serous glands.

questions.stem: A gland with purely serous acini, numerous intercalated ducts and fat cells in the stroma is the:
questions.why: Fat increases with age; the facial nerve runs through it.

notes.E: Serous, but not a salivary gland.

questions.stem: Most of the unstimulated (resting) saliva comes from the:
questions.why: About 60–70%; the parotid gives most stimulated saliva.

questions.stem: A ranula is a mucous retention cyst most often arising from the:
questions.why: Bluish swelling in the floor of the mouth.

questions.stem: The palatine tonsil lies between the:

options.label: B
options.text: soft palate and posterior pharyngeal wall

questions.why: In the tonsillar fossa of the oropharynx.
